JUDGMENT

The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.7,78,815/- for the damages caused to the vehicle bearing registration No.KA-57- F-2492 in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That, on 24.7.2022, KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-57-F-2492 on its scheduled route from Puducherry to Bengaluru and left Puducherry bus stand towards Bengaluru via Thiruvannamalai driven by its driver, when he reached near Gingee, opposite to BSNL office, Thiruvannamalai-Bengaluru road at about mid night 24 hour, the driver of the bus moving his bus extreme left side, at that time, the Tamilnadu registration bus bearing No.TN-25- BS-4964, driver of the bus came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the KSRTC bus right side front portion.
Therefore, KSRTC bus badly damaged.
3. It is further stated that, immediately after the accident, the bus was taken to Divisional work shop, Bengaluru central division for getting it repaired.
The said bus stood idle for 19 days.
The petitioner corporation arranged another bus to the route and shift passengers.
The material consumed for repairs amounts to Rs.55,257/- and lost its revenue due to idling of the bus amounts to Rs.7,23,558/-.
4. It is alleged in the petition that, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the Tamilnadu bus bearing No.TN-25-BS- 4964.
In this regard, case was registered against the driver by the jurisdictional Gingee Police in Crime No.361/2022 under section 279 & 337 of IPC.
As such, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition seeking compensation.
5. After registration of this case, notices were issued to the respondents.

In response to the notices,
the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court, remained absent, placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
6. In the written statement of the respondent No.2 has contended that petition is not maintainable in either in law or on facts and the same is liable to be dismissed in limine.
This respondent has admitted about the policy and its validity.
It is the contention of the respondent No.2 that the driver of the bus had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the said bus at the time of accident.
Further denied the manner of accident and also damages caused to the KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-57-F-2492.

It is also contention of the respondent No.2 that the compensation claimed by K.S.R.T.C vs Anbalagan N on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66733548/
2
the petitioner is excessive and exhorbitant.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

7. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following recasted issues;
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that, KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-57- F-2492 has damaged in an accident that occurred on 24.7.2022 at about 00-00 hours (24.00) a.m. near Shettyhalli, NH-75 road, Gingee, Opposite to BSNL office, Thiruvannamalai-Bengaluru road, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tamilnadu bus bearing registration No.TN-25-BS-4964?
2) Whether the petitioner proves that, KSRTC is the owner of the bus bearing registration No.KA-57-F-2492?
3) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate? from whom?
4) What order or award?

8. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioner, he has placed his affidavit evidence in lieu of examination-in-chief, who examined as PW1 and got marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P10.
9.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not adduced any rebuttal evidence in order to disprove the contention of the petitioner.

10. On appreciation of the evidence available on record, my findings to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative  Issue No.2: In the Affirmative  Issue No.3: Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4: As per final order  for the following:
 R E A S O N S ISSUE NO.1 & 2:-
11.
These two issues are taken together for common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts.

sentences.text: It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Tamilnadu bus bearing registration No.TN-25-BS-4964, the alleged accident had taken place, consequently bus belonging to the petitioner bearing registration No.KA-57-F-2492 caused damages.

Since the facts of the case has been narrated in detail above, once again narration of the petition and the defenses of the respondent No.2 forthcoming in the written statement is not required herein.
13. The petitioner in order to prove his case, examined himself as PW1.
In his examination-in- chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
To demonstrate the point of ownership placed R.C. extract as per Ex.P8 and F.C. as per Ex.P9.
On perusal of R.C. there is a clear mention about the name of the petitioner in connection with its vehicle and in the driving license Ex.P8 also fitness of the bus.
To disprove all these documents, no contra materials forthcoming in the evidence of the respondent.
14. Further the petitioner has relied upon Ex.P1 to Ex.P6.
Ex. P1- authorisation letter, Ex.P2- true copy of FIR in Cr.No.361/2022 of Gingee Police, Ex.P2(a)-translated copy of FIR.
Ex . P3
-FIS given by the driver of the KSRTC bus.
Ex.P3(a)-translated copy of FIS, Ex.P4-true copy of charge sheet in Cr. No.361/2022 of Gingee police, sketch and spot mahazar.
(Ex.P4(a)-translated copy of charge sheet, sketch and spot mahazar.
Ex. P5.
Thereafter, collected the report of the motor vehicle inspector as per Ex.P5.
In the opinion of the motor vehicle inspector, accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles involved in the accident.

Further, in connection with the vehicle of the petitioner, IMV report shows the damages viz., "front windscreen glass broken, front body sheet right side damaged, front right side driver door damaged, steering column bend, right side mirror broken, right side one fixed glass broken".

Further Ex.P6 in connection with the bus bearing No.TN-25-BS-4964 shows "front left side door damaged, front left side two fixed glass broken, front bumper damaged, front cowl damaged, front windscreen glass broken, front both head light damaged, front right side driver door damaged, right side four fixed glass broken, dash board damaged, driver partition damaged, roof front portion damaged, steering column damaged,
accelerator pedal bend."

15. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by the driver of the KSRTC bus, the S.H.O. of Gingee Police have registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Sections 279 of I.P.C.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offence punishable under section 279 of IPC.
16.
At the time of cross-examination of PW1, admitted that, Rs.14,306/- labour costs mentioned in Ex.P7 has not paid to the staff.
Except this, nothing has been elicited from the mouth of the PW1 to prove the contention of the respondent regarding rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Hence, it is crystal clear from the evidence available on record that, due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, the vehicle belonged to the petitioner was damaged and the petitioner is the owner of the KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-57-F-2492.

sentences.text: In the light of my discussions held above, I am of the view that, the evidence of the PW1 and the documentary evidence placed by the petitioner substantiate the case of the petitioner.

Hence, I am of the opinion that, petitioner has proved its case that, the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle Tamilnadu bus vehicle bearing registration No.TN- 25-BS-4964.

In the said accident, the KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-57-F-2492,
belonged to the petitioner was damaged.
Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.1 & 2 are in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3 :
18.
The petitioner being the owner of the defending KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-57- F-2492, asserting that, after the accident vehicle in question belonged to the petitioner was fully damaged.

As per Ex.P5-IMV Report reveals that "front windscreen glass broken, front body sheet right side damaged, front right side driver door damaged, steering column bend, right side mirror broken, right side one fixed glass broken".

To substantiate its contention PW1 has placed Ex.P7- repair cost at Rs.28,782/-.
19.

At the time of argument the counsel for the petitioner has argued that, during the period of repair of the vehicle from 24.7.2022 to 12.8.2022, the usual course of its routine operation, the petitioner corporation was getting income of Rs.38,082/- per day.

Since the bus has been kept idle,
the income from the said bus has been lost to the petitioner-corporation.
In fact the petitioner is paying interest on the amount borrowed for securing the vehicle.
Hence, the petitioner is liable for getting idling charges amountint to Rs.7,23,558/-.
To substantiate the said fact, petitioner has placed income report from 1.4.2022 to 30.9.2022 at Ex.P10.

In this regard the counsel for the petitioner has relied the following decision of the Hon'ble High Court in case of the Managing Director KSRTC Vs. United Insurance Co. Ltd., & Others in MFA No.4377/2001 Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka awarded the compensation for idling period for loss of earnings from that damaged bus.
20.

On the other hand the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 relied the following decisions;
1) MFA No. 23362/2012 between North-West Karnataka Transport Corporation, Gokul Road,
Hubbali Vs. Mrs. VVGN Prasad Guptha & Others.
2) MFA 6461/2014 between National Insurance CO. Ltd., Vs. Sr. Divisional Controller KSRTC Mangaluru Division Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that "in the case of KSRTC where they are operating many hundred number of buses and obtaining permits from the transport authorities and it is obligatory on the part of them according to the permit issued, they have to maintain reserve bus/spare bus and in any contingent event they have to operate spare bus/reserved bus

sentences.text: In the instant case, on perusal of the cross- examination of PW1, it clearly reveals that KSRTC has send the spare bus on its scheduled route as usual, under such event, there would not be loss of revenue, because reserve bus is operating on the same route.
Therefore, KSRTC is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of revenue or idling charges.
Hence, the decision relied by the respondent No.2 is aptly applicable to the facts of this case.

22. On going through the recitals of the Ex.P7 along with the appreciation of the evidence given by the PW1 and by taking into consideration of damages mentioned in Ex.P5, it is just and proper to award Rs.28,782/- towards the damages of the vehicle.

23. In the light of my detailed discussions held above, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.28,782/- (Rupees twenty eight thousand seven hundred and eighty two only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition, till the realization of the award amount.

LIABILITY:
24.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Tamilnadu bus bearing registration No.TN-25-BS- 4964, alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.
As such, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
25. As per the records insurance policy was valid from 19.11.2021 to 18.11.2022.
The alleged accident had taken place on 24.7.2022.

As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.2 being the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.3 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.4:
26.

In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.28,782/- (Rupees twenty eight thousand seven hundred and eighty two only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
